In mathematics, a '''harmonic morphism''' is a (smooth) map <math>\phi:(M^m,g)\to (N^n,h)</math> between [[Riemannian manifold]]s that pulls back real-valued [[harmonic function]]s on the [[codomain]] to harmonic functions on the domain. Harmonic morphisms form a special class of [[harmonic map]]s, namely those that are horizontally (weakly) conformal.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|url=http://ukcatalogue.oup.com/product/9780198503620.do|title=Harmonic Morphisms Between Riemannian Manifolds|work=Oxford University Press}}</ref>

In local coordinates, <math>x</math> on <math>M</math> and <math>y</math> on <math>N</math>, the '''harmonicity''' of <math>\phi</math> is expressed by the [[non-linear]] system

:<math>\tau(\phi )=\sum_{i,j=1}^m g^{ij}\left(\frac{\partial^2\phi^{\gamma}}{\partial x_i\partial x_j}
-\sum_{k=1}^m\hat\Gamma^k_{ij}\frac{\partial\phi^{\gamma}}{\partial x_k}
+\sum_{\alpha,\beta=1}^n\Gamma^{\gamma}_{\alpha\beta}\circ\phi
\frac{\partial\phi^{\alpha}}{\partial x_i}
\frac{\partial\phi^{\beta }}{\partial x_j} \right)=0,</math> 

where <math>\phi^\alpha=y_\alpha\circ\phi</math> and <math>\hat\Gamma,\Gamma</math> are the [[Christoffel symbols]] on <math>M</math> and <math>N</math>, respectively.  The '''horizontal conformality''' is given by 

:<math>\sum_{i,j=1}^mg^{ij}(x)\frac{\partial\phi^\alpha}{\partial x_i}(x)\frac{\partial\phi^\beta }{\partial x_j}(x)=\lambda^2(x)h^{\alpha\beta}(\phi(x)),</math>

where the conformal factor <math>\lambda:M\to\mathbb R_0^+</math> is a continuous function called the [[dilation (metric space)|dilation]]. Harmonic morphisms are therefore solutions to [[non-linear]] [[over-determined system]]s of [[partial differential equations]], determined by the geometric data of the [[manifold]]s involved.  For this reason, they  are difficult to find and have no general existence theory, not even locally.  

== Complex analysis ==

When the [[codomain]] of <math>\phi:(M,g)\to (N^2,h)</math> is a [[surface (topology)|surface]], the system of [[partial differential equation]]s that we are dealing with, is invariant under conformal changes of the metric <math>h</math>.  This means that, at least for local studies, the [[codomain]] can be chosen to be the [[complex plane]] with its standard flat metric.  In this situation a complex-valued [[function (mathematics)|function]]  <math>\phi=u+iv:(M,g)\to\mathbb C</math> is a harmonic morphisms if and only if 

:<math>\Delta_M(\phi)=\Delta_M (u)+i\Delta_M (v)=0</math>

and

:<math>g(\nabla\phi,\nabla\phi )=\|\nabla u\|^2-\|\nabla v\|^2+2ig(\nabla u,\nabla v)=0.</math>

This means that we look for two real-valued [[harmonic function]]s <math>u,v:(M,g)\to\mathbb R</math> with [[gradient]]s <math>\nabla u,\nabla v</math> that are orthogonal and of the same norm at each point.  This shows that complex-valued harmonic morphisms <math>\phi:(M,g)\to\mathbb C</math> from [[Riemannian manifold]]s generalise [[holomorphic function]]s <math>f:(M,g,J)\to\mathbb C</math> from [[Kähler manifold]]s and possess many of their highly interesting properties. The theory of harmonic morphisms can therefore be seen as a generalisation of [[complex analysis]].<ref name="autogenerated1"/>

== Minimal surfaces ==

In [[differential geometry]], one is interested in constructing minimal [[submanifold]]s of a given ambient space <math>(M,g)</math>.  Harmonic morphisms are useful tools for this purpose.  This is due to the fact that every regular fibre <math>\phi^{-1}(\{z_0\})</math> of such a map <math>\phi:(M,g)\to (N^2,h)</math> with values in a [[surface (topology)|surface]] is a minimal submanifold of the domain with codimension 2.<ref name="autogenerated1"/> This gives an attractive method for manufacturing whole families of [[minimal surface]]s in 4-dimensional [[manifold]]s <math>(M^4,g)</math>, in particular,   [[homogeneous spaces]], such as [[Lie group]]s and [[symmetric space]]s.{{Citation needed|date=September 2020}}

== Examples ==

* Identity and constant maps are harmonic morphisms.
* [[Holomorphic function]]s in the [[complex plane]] are harmonic morphisms.
* [[Holomorphic function]]s in the [[complex vector space]] <math>\mathbb C^n</math> are harmonic morphisms.
* [[Holomorphic map]]s from [[Kähler manifold]]s with values in a [[Riemann surface]] are harmonic morphisms.
* The [[Hopf map]]s <math>\phi:S^3\to S^2</math>, <math>\phi:S^7\to S^4</math> and <math>\phi:S^{15}\to S^8</math> are harmonic morphisms.
* For [[compact Lie group]]s <math>K\subset H\subset G</math> the standard Riemannian [[fibration]] <math>\phi:G/H\to G/K</math> is a harmonic morphism.
* [[Riemannian submersion]]s with minimal fibres are harmonic morphisms.
